01Pre-shipment review

Before the equipment leaves.

Pre-shipment review connects the electrical configuration with the equipment, packages and information to be handed over.

  1. Equipment scope

    Match the supplied configuration with the project equipment and accessory scope.

  2. Inspection and acceptance

    Coordinate factory inspection, agreed testing and inspection records.

  3. Packages and shipping marks

    Align equipment, spare parts, packing-list entries and package identification.

  4. Document handover

    Organise electrical drawings, operating instructions and inspection information for the receiving team.

02Packing & marking

Equipment and spare parts, organised together.

Packing lists and shipping marks connect each package with its equipment or spare-part scope.

  • Equipment

    Identify the supplied equipment and its accessories in the project scope.

  • Spare parts

    Organise spare parts with their own packing-list entries.

  • Shipping marks

    Keep package identification aligned with handover and destination coordination.

03Technical package

The technical package travels with the project.

Engineering information supports equipment receiving, installation and operation. The document package keeps electrical interfaces, equipment arrangement and operating guidance connected.

Discuss your project requirements

  • Electrical design

    Single-line diagrams and control interfaces

  • Equipment arrangement

    Outline and foundation information

  • Operating guidance

    Bilingual use and operating instructions

  • Protection

    Project protection-setting information

  • Verification

    Inspection and factory-test records

04Operation support

Support continues into operation.

Technical coordination follows the equipment configuration and the project’s service scope.

Installation and commissioning

Installation guidance, operating instructions and technical coordination support equipment integration and commissioning.

Operation and maintenance

Service procedures support equipment enquiries, operation guidance and maintenance coordination.

Spare-part requirements

Share the equipment details and the part required so the technical team can coordinate the matching requirement.

Operator training

Training covers equipment use, maintenance, repair and emergency handling, with practical demonstrations aligned to the service scope.

Completion and follow-up

Service work is recorded and reviewed with the project team and customer site contact before departure. Unresolved or exceptional issues are escalated for a coordinated action plan and follow-up.

05Service requests

What happens after a service request?

Our service procedure defines separate milestones for recording, accepting and planning a request.

  1. Within 2 h

    Record the request

    Service information is entered into the service system within 2 hours of receipt.

  2. Within 2 h

    Confirm the requirement

    The responsible unit accepts the request and contacts the customer within 2 hours of assignment.

  3. Within ½ working day

    Prepare the initial plan

    Personnel, materials and the initial service plan are arranged within half a working day of acceptance.

  4. Within 2 h

    Coordinate the visit

    After receiving the work order, the assigned engineer contacts the customer within 2 hours to discuss the scope and anticipated arrival.

These are request-handling milestones, not guaranteed arrival or repair times. Site access, travel and the agreed service scope determine visit arrangements.

Have these details ready

  • EquipmentModel, serial number and a readable nameplate photo
  • LocationSite, country and the on-site contact
  • Support neededCommissioning, maintenance, training or a replacement part
  • Current conditionSymptoms, alarm records and relevant photos, where safe to obtain
